sources.title: EVGA RTX 3060 XC Black teardown
sources.applicability: explicitly_EVGA_RTX_3060_XC_Black

findings: Four spring-loaded cooler mounting screws pass through the PCB around the GPU. This is a distinct four-screw GPU mount group.
A separate pair of screws secures the fin-stack base to the board; the presenter describes them as 'a couple'. Their exact positions are not mapped.

I/O-plate removal exposes two narrower screws with a nut on the opposite side of each, followed by three smaller display-output retaining screws. The presenter selects a Phillips #0 driver for the three display-output screws.
Both fan leads are separate connectors with release clips; disconnect them before lifting/separating the cooler.
technical_observations.limitations: The teardown exposes several distinct hardware groups but does not provide a calibrated screw map or a one-to-one mapping to Tom's Hardware's eight-screw cooler/shroud aggregate. Do not sum the four GPU mounts, fin-stack base pair, I/O screw/nut pair, display-output screws and Tom's Hardware count as one total. No thread, length, torque or complete removal order is supplied.

findings: Two thermal-pad thickness observations are spoken: about 2.0 mm for one pad and approximately 1.5 mm for another; the second is explicitly described as harder to measure.
The presenter counts two central heatpipe tubes running through the GPU contact plate and estimates approximately 6 mm tube diameter.
The copper GPU cold plate contacts the die directly; it is joined to the fin stack, and the pipes return through the copper plate toward the memory-side region.
Six GDDR6 positions are visible, arranged three along one side and three along the other; some pipe runs cross the memory region without direct memory contact.
technical_observations.limitations: The narration does not assign the 2.0 mm and 1.5 mm observations to specific memory/VRM locations or package footprints. Heatpipe tube-loop count and exposed tube-run count are different possible counting conventions; do not collapse them without a drawing.

findings: The presenter identifies a row of MOSFETs contacted by a copper plate.
Two inductors are discussed on the opposite-side power area; the presenter tentatively calls that area the memory VRM, so that functional assignment remains tentative.
The presenter notes a thermal-pad impression on the two-inductor area but says pad contact is incomplete for the rest of the nearby inductors.
Each fan is retained by three screws and has its own independently replaceable lead.
Additional shroud screws are pointed out during fan removal, but the presenter is unsure whether the group contains four or six; no exact shroud fastener count is accepted.
technical_observations.limitations: No MOSFET part number, inductor designation, inductance, VRM phase topology, controller identity, pad footprint or screw coordinates are provided. The shroud fastener count is explicitly uncertain and must remain a candidate, not a numeric claim.

findings: Two current-sense shunts are discussed: one associated with the auxiliary power-input path and a separate one associated with PCIe-slot 12 V.
The presenter states a 5 milliohm shunt on the auxiliary power-input path; do not copy that value to the separate slot shunt.
A fuse is visible for input-protection troubleshooting.
The cleaned GPU die marking is read as NVIDIA GA106-300-A1.
technical_observations.limitations: The transcript does not provide fuse part number/rating, shunt reference designators, calibrated electrical nets or the resistance of the slot shunt.

sources.title: EVGA GeForce RTX 3060 XC teardown with 12G-P5-3655-KR sample label
sources.applicability: The article body describes an EVGA RTX 3060 XC teardown. The rear-PCB identity photograph on the article's main page visibly reads P/N 12G-P5-3655-KR, the exact XC BLACK retail SKU. On the teardown page, Tom's Hardware reports eight cooler/shroud retention screws (four around the GPU and four near the far end), two fan connections, and six Samsung K4ZAF325BM-HC16 GDDR6 chips rated for 16Gbps. The photograph ties the teardown sample to the retail SKU; exact screw coordinates, package-to-net mapping and PCB revision remain unverified.
sources.identity_locator: Main review's EVGA rear-PCB photo: label reads P/N 12G-P5-3655-KR.

sources.title: EVGA232 / PG190-A02 GA104-GA106 GPU schematic — unverified community-hosted candidate
sources.applicability: The community file name includes EVGA232 / RTX 2070 / RTX3060 / PG190-A02 / GA104-GA106, but the document text itself carries NVIDIA drawing number 600-1G190-BASE-A02, PCB revision PG190-A02 and BOM revision A dated 2020-06-12. Its text-layer block diagram lists NVVDD-PH1 through PH8 and FBVDDQ-PH1/PH2; this is a reference-board topology only. The PDF does not mention retail SKU 12G-P5-3655-KR or the EVGA232 silkscreen. It must not be used to assert phase count, net routing, values or pinout for the XC BLACK until a physical-board correlation is established. Rendered-page screenshots could not be fetched during this audit, so no page artwork or component-value extraction is claimed.
sources.use_policy: Reference-only. Do not use its reference design to populate the exact EVGA XC BLACK VRM phase count, component inventory, PCB routing, BOM or service map. The title of a third-party index is not proof of board equivalence. No PDF pages or third-party assets are redistributed.

sources.title: NVIDIA Ampere GA10x GPU architecture whitepaper
sources.applicability: GA10x architecture-common SM and TPC organization: 128 CUDA cores, four third-generation Tensor Cores, four texture units, one second-generation RT Core, 256 KB register file, 128 KB L1/shared memory per SM; two SMs and one PolyMorph Engine per TPC. Applied only as logical architecture to GA106 RTX 3060. The GA102 physical floorplan and GPC layout are not transferred.

sources.title: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3060 review — EVGA XC Black Gaming cooler summary

sources.title: EVGA GeForce RTX 3060 XC Gaming replacement fan listing
sources.applicability: Aftermarket seller listing names fan code PLA09215S12H and advertises broad EVGA RTX 3050/3060/3060 Ti XC-family compatibility, including XC BLACK. The listing's claimed 90 mm size, 12 V, 0.55 A, 4-pin connector and 42 mm mounting spacing are seller specifications only. No original fan label or exact-card fitment measurement has been verified.

sources.title: EVGA RTX 3050 / 3060 / 3060 Ti XC Gaming Black replacement fan listing
sources.applicability: Aftermarket replacement listing advertises broad compatibility across multiple EVGA XC Gaming Black variants and lists PLA09215S12H-family fans. The catalog material gives an approximately 87 mm size and 15 mm / 20 mm depth variants, plus seller-claimed 12 V, 0.55 A, 4-pin and 42 mm mounting spacing. These are catalogue claims, not an OEM label or confirmed fitment for 12G-P5-3655-KR; its dimensions also differ from another seller's 90 mm claim.

sources.title: EVGA GeForce RTX 3060 XC BLACK GAMING 12G-P5-3655-KR — product photo gallery
sources.applicability: The listing title and model field identify exact part number 12G-P5-3655-KR. Two front product photographs show eight visible impeller blade surfaces on each fan. Retained for visible blade count only; these images are not an OEM mechanical drawing or inspection of an installed sample. Blade pitch, camber, exact profile, thickness, depth and fan OEM identity remain unverified.

sources.title: EVGA official product specifications — GeForce RTX 3060 XC BLACK GAMING 12G-P5-3655-KR
sources.applicability: Explicitly identifies retail part number 12G-P5-3655-KR as GeForce RTX 3060 XC BLACK GAMING. Publishes whole-card dimensions 201.8 × 110 mm and dual-slot width, but does not publish bare-PCB dimensions, component coordinates, BoardView, or cooler service data.

sources.title: ThermalPad.eu EVGA RTX 3060 XC family pad-size guide — excluded due source conflict
sources.applicability: The page attributes 40 × 15 × 2 mm strips for two three-module banks plus an additional 25 × 15 × 2 mm two-module strip to the RTX 3060 XC. Its linked Reddit source is a thread about 3060 Ti XC pads, and commenters explicitly correct the model distinction: the 3060 XC has two banks of three VRAM modules, while the 3060 Ti XC adds the two-module group. Because the page appears to reverse or conflate these variants, none of its pad sizes or contact-zone assignments is accepted for 12G-P5-3655-KR.

sources.title: Community discussion correcting RTX 3060 XC versus RTX 3060 Ti XC thermal-pad context
sources.applicability: The thread title concerns 3060 Ti XC thermal-pad sizing. A comment explicitly corrects an earlier mix-up: the Gamers Nexus teardown was RTX 3060 XC; the 3060 XC shows two banks of three VRAM packages, while the 3060 Ti XC adds a further two-module group. Community discussion is used only to flag the linked ThermalPad.eu guide as internally conflicted; it is not a primary pad measurement or an exact 12G-P5-3655-KR service specification.

sources.title: Hardware Asylum EVGA RTX 3060 XC Gaming cooler and PCB teardown
sources.applicability: The page describes an EVGA RTX 3060 XC Gaming sample but does not identify retail part number 12G-P5-3655-KR. It discusses a pair of U-shaped heatpipes, VRM cooling, apparently unpopulated phase pads and PCB airflow cutout. These are family/variant observations only and are not transferred to the XC BLACK target's heatpipe loop count, VRM phase topology, PCB layout or coordinates.

sources.title: TechPowerUp EVGA GeForce RTX 3060 XC circuit-board analysis
sources.applicability: The reviewed card is labelled EVGA GeForce RTX 3060 XC, with no verified 12G-P5-3655-KR sample identity. The page reports a 5-phase GPU rail with uPI uP9512R, Alpha & Omega DrMOS, a 2-phase memory rail with uPI uP1666Q and M3828N memory MOSFETs, and Samsung GDDR6 marking. These are family-variant candidates only; do not assign any controller, phase count, MOSFET, memory-rail topology or PCB coordinate to the XC BLACK target without an exact-board sample match.

sources.title: Badcaps NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3060 schematic and BoardView discussion

Treat any referenced board files as unrelated candidates until their silkscreen and revision are correlated to a physical target sample.

sources.title: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3060 Review: EVGA XC BLACK Tested
sources.applicability: Explicitly identifies the reviewed product as EVGA GeForce RTX 3060 12GB XC BLACK. Reports a single Metro Exodus 2160/high operating observation in an open case: approximately 24 °C ambient, 68.1 °C GPU temperature (80.5 °C hotspot), fans at 73% / ~2030 RPM, and peak observed board power 172.4 W. The page does not publish retail part number 12G-P5-3655-KR; these are sample/workload measurements, not fan maximum RPM, factory fan curve, nominal board limit or universally repeatable operating values.

sources.title: eBay aftermarket fan listing with PLD09220S12HH compatibility claim
sources.applicability: Seller title advertises a PLD09220S12HH replacement fan for EVGA RTX 3060 / 3060 Ti XC BLACK family cards. The listing identifies the brand as Unbranded and compatible brand generically as EVGA RTX3060 / 3060ti XC; this is a broad aftermarket compatibility assertion, not an OEM part label for retail SKU 12G-P5-3655-KR. Do not assign PLD09220S12HH to the target card's original fan.
